title: Indonesians protest government response to wildfires in Jakarta

tea.why: Protesters are angry over wildfires and a toxic haze that has made thousands unwell for weeks.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand that authorities extinguish the fires immediately and declare a state of emergency.
tea.changed: Oct 21: Police detained six activists who draped Greenpeace banners from a roundabout monument in Jakarta.

summary: Demonstrators gathered in several cities across Indonesia, including Jakarta, Bandung, Yogyakarta, Pekanbaru, and Makassar, to protest against the government's handling of an ongoing wildfire and toxic haze crisis. The actions were organised by students to express dissatisfaction with President Prabowo Subianto's administration on its second anniversary, citing perceived ineptitude and corruption in failing to extinguish blazes that have burned vast swaths of Sumatra and Borneo. Protesters demanded immediate action to put out the fires and called for a state of emergency. In response, the National Disaster Mitigation Agency stated that more than 60,000 firefighters and 49 aircraft were deployed for dousing and cloud seeding efforts.
response: National Disaster Mitigation Agency spokesman Berton Panjaitan stated that over 60,000 firefighters and volunteers were deployed countrywide alongside 49 aircraft for water bombing and cloud seeding. Police also detained six activists in Jakarta.

arrests.text: Police detained six activists who had draped Greenpeace protest banners from a monument

updates.text: Residents in Palangkaraya protested on Monday to demand the declaration of a state of emergency.
Police detained six activists who draped Greenpeace banners from a monument on Jakarta's central Bundaran HI roundabout.
Students held demonstrations in Jakarta, Bandung, Yogyakarta, Pekanbaru, and Makassar.
